My wife is a working woman. She is ambitious, focused and independent. She
takes up responsibility without complaining (at work & at home) She tells me
stories about her office & I get to know so much about another organization.
She is a wonderful cook and manages home in a way I can never imagine (she is
a magician) She travels 2 hours a day to reach office. We rarely get time for
us during weekdays. Recently, she had to go to a different city for training
(3 months). It was tough to be away. But, it was important for her career
growth so we had to do it. She had to manage everything alone and she did
happily. I try to be supportive, understand her and help wherever I can. She
is an inspiration to her cousin sisters who are in school and all young girls
who want to be independent. She is living the dream her mother and my mother
(as they never got a chance to work) She makes all of us proud every day.
hashtag#Women are half the population And if they are away from the workforce,
we are missing on so much. I feel inspired by people who push boundaries and
lead by example. My wife inspires me to live life more every day.

what is the difference? Why it is okay to drive a car but not okay to use deep
learning model? Because EVERYONE drives a car and not EVERYONE uses deep
learning. That’s the only difference.

I observe a visible frustration among beginners in terms of what to learn in
data science and not. It's pretty obvious since the frantic pace at which new
knowledge is being created in this space and new libraries being introduced by
the tech giants, it really leads to immense disillusionment among all and a
sense of being left behind. I have a simple suggestion. Unplug! Be driven by
"your" problem statement and not what the world is solving. If your problem is
getting solved by simple SQL no need to worry about Spark. Learn image
processing first rather than getting suffocated with libraries over libraries.
Understand simple text processing techniques before worrying about fasttext,
Glove or BERT. Go Slow, but master the skills which will help you solve the
problem you have on your table. Relax, just don't fizzle out!
hashtag#datascience hashtag#machinelearning hashtag#problemsolving

I see a habit of few data scientist taking data, fitting simple models and if
accuracy is low immediately jumping on to complex models Try below 2 steps
before moving to trendy and complex algorithms Follow your model output ->
Listen to what your algorithm metrics says. Drill down into misclassification
scenarios and see if you are able to find any interesting pattern Be Curious
and Creative with your data -> Try to see if you find any pattern or
relationship in data that has ability to influence your model outcome. Lot can
be solved by proper EDA and feature engineering These 2 steps are key to
analyze any model performance, be it simple or complex Be a Data Detective,
follow data prints, collect evidences of interactions with the target and make
the data confess on the objective If you are still not meeting accuracy go for
complex models in increments. The steps you performed above is still relevant
and can be input to your complex models to enhance decision boundary In some
critical business process 84% of simple model performance might be better than
86% of complex models hashtag#datascience hashtag#ai hashtag#ml
hashtag#machinelearning hashtag#artificialintelligence hashtag#datascientist
